clue.text: Sailor twice produces battle-axe

indicators.note: twice tells us the word for sailor is written two times in a row

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman's doubling-up somehow yields a formidable old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A battle-axe is also a domineering, bad-tempered woman, the sense needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for a fierce, overbearing woman, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Ecstasy comes from nectar being drunk

indicators.note: being drunk suggests staggering, so the letters of nectar reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Bliss arrives after downing the drink of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy and this word both name a rapt, dreamlike state of mind, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Practised and tried again covering empty space

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: a case reheard in court has been tried again

indicators.note: empty means the word space loses its insides, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone has drilled and retried, filling up a vacant gap.
explanation.walkthrough: A court case heard a second time has been tried again, which is why 'tried again' fits; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a performance is to go through it beforehand, a synonym here in the past tense.

clue.text: One hears foreign car going over hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over puts the car above the hill, so it comes first

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A German saloon climbs over a rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on the moors of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin audire means to hear, so a listener is literally one who hears; an accounts examiner originally heard them read aloud.

clue.text: Penniless, goes back to pick up penny

indicators.note: to pick up means the reversed word takes the next letter into itself
back means the word for goes is read in reverse

parts.note: departs means goes, leaves

explanation.surface: A broke person returns to collect a single coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEPARTS into STRAPED, and 'to pick up' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of cash, informally, is a synonym of having no money.

clue.text: Not sure Queen's consumed by fashion

indicators.note: consumed by means the queen's letter is swallowed inside the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or style
R, from Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Doubt over whether the monarch has been swept up by trends.
explanation.walkthrough: TON, as in 'the ton', means high fashion; R is Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Being torn between options means being undecided, a synonym of unsure.

clue.text: Tab made from tobacco, untipped

indicators.note: made from says the answer is formed out of letters running through the next words

explanation.surface: A cigarette made from filterless tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tab' is slang for a cigarette, which fits the surface but here means a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab at a bar is a running bill, the same as a credit arrangement with a shop.

clue.text: Projection of short programme with new content

indicators.note: content means the letter for new sits inside the shortened word
short means programme is cut down to its familiar clipped form

explanation.surface: Previewing a brief broadcast with fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips 'programme' to PROG; 'with new content' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine of a fork is a pointed projection, so the word is a specific example.

clue.text: Make public record on waste

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the record above the next piece

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
to lose an opportunity is to waste it

explanation.surface: Reveal the contents of a recording about squandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal information is to make it known, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Part of flytrap hid some bugs

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A carnivorous plant has concealed a few insects inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects, examples of bugs.

clue.text: Beloved is faithful without urgency occasionally

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the devout word goes around the rest

parts.note: pious means faithful, devout

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of urgency is used

explanation.surface: A loved one is loyal and never in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes REC from u-R-g-E-n-C-y; 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear or treasured is held in great affection, a synonym of beloved.

clue.text: Charlie rushed to accept sex, not displaying this

definitions.text: Charlie rushed to accept sex, not displaying this

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to accept means the word for rushed takes another inside it

parts.note: hasty means rushed
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: An eager Charlie hurried into bed, plainly lacking a certain virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a man rushing to accept sex is not showing this virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from sexual activity is the very virtue Charlie fails to show.

clue.text: Newspaper covers singular robberies

indicators.note: in a down clue, covers places the paper on top of the next letter

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A paper reports on remarkable thefts.
explanation.walkthrough: THE FT is the Financial Times; 'singular' tempts as 'remarkable' but is S.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of stealing are robberies, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Copper directed to return holding golf club

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: holding means the reversed word wraps around the letter for golf
to return means the word for directed is read backwards

parts.note: led means directed, guided
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A police officer is sent back carrying a golfing iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns LED into DEL, and 'holding' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thick stick used as a weapon is a club, a synonym.

clue.text: Spot Greek character around end of alphabet

indicators.note: around means the Greek letter surrounds the final letter

parts.note: sigma is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of alphabet is taken

explanation.surface: Find a Greek letter near omega, at the alphabet's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of alphabet' tempts as Z or omega but is T, the last letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or blemish on reputation is a spot, in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Clandestine pursuit Tories abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned in the sense of wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A secret chase that the Conservatives gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservative party; 'abandoned' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret and stealthy dealings are clandestine, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Upset husband in public squabble

indicators.note: in means the husband's letter is placed inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: overt means open, public
a row is a squabble

explanation.surface: A husband caught up in a very public argument gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a government is to bring it down, a synonym of upset in its overturning sense.

clue.text: Girl embracing very French lover

indicators.note: embracing means the word for girl hugs the French word

parts.note: a miss is a girl
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: A young woman hugging her extremely Gallic paramour.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in an illicit relationship with a married man is a kept lover.

clue.text: One feeling bad at poorly patient

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: poorly means the letters of the phrase are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell is sick at a hospital patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like a noun for the sick person but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tireless persistence is a form of patience, so the words are near-synonyms.

clue.text: Toady is comparatively prostrate

definitions.meaning: to toady is to fawn on someone with insincere praise
more horizontal, more level than something else

explanation.surface: A sycophant who grovels lower than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to praise insincerely; as a comparative it means more level or horizontal.

clue.text: For the audience, more progressive rock?

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: bolder means more daring and progressive

explanation.surface: A question of whether some music is more experimental prog rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'progressive rock' looks like a music genre; 'rock' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large rounded stone is a specific kind of rock.

clue.text: Club supporter's gutted, say

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment, with the possessive s

indicators.note: gutted means the word say loses its inside, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A football fan is devastated, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves SY from 'say'. A brassie, also spelt this way, is an old wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for a number two wood used in golf, an example of a club.

clue.text: God having a cross on chest

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A deity wearing a crucifix on his breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the body between neck and abdomen is the chest, the anatomical term.

clue.text: Main objection concerns easily acquired nausea primarily

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: The chief complaint is about readily caught sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective but is the old poetic noun for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open sea.

clue.text: Boasting about American's support

indicators.note: about means the boasting word goes around the letter for American

parts.note: bluster is loud boastful talk

explanation.surface: Bragging regarding a Yank's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post holding up a rail is an upright support.

clue.text: Naked except for sweetheart

parts.note: bar means except for, as in all bar one
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, e

explanation.surface: Unclothed, apart from a beloved companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed and uncovered are synonyms, as are naked and this word.

clue.text: Final passage in European Union the French rejected

indicators.note: in means the passage sits inside the union's letters

parts.note: a vent is a passage for air

indicators.note: rejected means the French word is turned back

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: The French refused the final passage of legislation in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LA, French for 'the', into AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate or ensuing at last, so final in the sense of happening in the end.

clue.text: Loves a party with others getting cut

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: getting cut means the word for others loses its tail letter

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a gathering where everyone else is excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting cut' trims REST to RES.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or be devoted to someone is to love them deeply, a synonym.

clue.text: Stuff Romeo found in small briefs, perhaps

indicators.note: found in means the letter for Romeo sits inside the following words

parts.note: briefs are one kind of undies, underwear
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lover discovered in tiny underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefs, perhaps' suggests lawyers' cases but means underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous small items or odds and ends are stuff, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Tired words ruined day at last

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of words are wrecked and rearranged
at last means only the final letter of day is used

explanation.surface: Weary words spoiled the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy and weary are near-synonyms, both describing a lack of energy.
